samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` — the whole housekeeping runtime — has no test of any kind
samples.evidence: Glob `packages/frontend/**/*offline-runtime*` returns only the source file; grep for `OfflineRuntime|offerRecoverableWork|rememberOfflineUser` across packages/frontend matches only offline-erase.ts/.test.ts (the helper), the component itself, and PrivateRoute.tsx. Nothing exercises: (a) `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` being called on mount — which is the *only* thing that makes `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` find an identity, so a regression here silently leaves document content on a shared device after sign-out while every offline-erase.test.ts case still passes (they call `rememberOfflineUser` themselves); (b) `watchForOfflineDisable(() => store, () => userId)` being installed at all, i.e. the Settings promise "turning it off deletes them"; (c) the once-per-session `collectStale()` sweep; (d) `offerRecoverableWork` — the loop that decides *not* to auto-create, skips keys `describeArchivedDocument` cannot read, dedupes by toast id, honours the `cancelled()` getter across awaits, and routes via `getDocumentPath`. The individual leaves (`recoverOfflineCopy`, `describeArchivedDocument`, `watchForOfflineDisable`) are well tested; the orchestration that actually invokes them on a real session is not.

samples.summary: The `eraseLocalData: false` guard on the 401 path — and `logout()`'s erase call — are untested
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` only covers 401 redirect de-duplication (grep for `erase|offline|401` returns lines 4-56, all about the redirect burst); no test in the repo asserts that the 401 arm of `fetchWithAuth` passes `eraseLocalData: false`. The diff's own comment states this is load-bearing: an involuntary expiry must not delete "the archives that hold changes the server never took", which are by design the only remaining copy of unreconciled work. A regression flipping that default destroys user work on a routine cookie expiry, and nothing would fail. Symmetrically, no test asserts `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` before redirecting, or that a failing erase cannot fail the sign-out — `offline-erase.test.ts` tests the helper in isolation, never the caller.

samples.summary: `removeMember`'s `isOfflineUser` cross-account guard and `deleteWorkspace`'s pre-delete listing have no tests
samples.evidence: Grep for `isOfflineUser|documentIdsIn` across packages/frontend matches only `lib/offline-erase.ts` and `api/workspaces.ts` — no test file. There is no `api/workspaces.test.ts` (Glob `packages/frontend/**/workspaces*.test.ts*` finds nothing; `app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx` is a component test). The guard the code documents at length — an owner removing *somebody else* must purge nothing, because the store is scoped to whoever is signed in on this device — is exactly the kind of inverted condition that deletes this user's local copies (including unsent work) of documents they still have every right to read, with no visible symptom. Likewise nothing pins that `documentIdsIn` is called *before* the access-ending DELETE, which is the only reason the purge can find anything.

samples.summary: No test that `deleteDocuments` purges only server-confirmed ids, or that `deleteDocument` purges only on `ok`
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` line 133-145 is the only `deleteDocuments` case; it mocks `okJson({ deleted: ['a'] })` and asserts the URL, method, body and returned value — nothing about `purgeOfflineDocuments`. Line 112 calls `deleteDocument` purely to check id encoding. So the rule the diff added and justifies in a comment — purge only what the server reports deleted, because "dropping the local copy of a document that is still there would delete unsent work the user can still push" — has zero coverage. A regression to `purgeOfflineDocuments(ids)` (the requested ids) on a partial-failure response silently destroys unsent local work and the suite stays green.

samples.summary: The chip's new call-to-action is only asserted as a label string; nothing tests that it works or that it is correctly gated
samples.evidence: Grep for `button|click|offerOffline|setOfflinePersistenceEnabled|Turn on for later` in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` returns only two comment lines. The one new test ('never promises to save the changes it is shown beside') reads `warning.mock.calls[0][1].action.label` and asserts it does not start with /^save / and matches /later/ — a copy assertion only. Untested: that clicking the chip (or the toast action) actually calls `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(true)`; that `offerOffline` is false when `supportsClientKey()` is false or the preference is already on (so no dead offer appears on a build that cannot honour it); that the chip renders as a `<button>` only in that state and stays a `<span>` otherwise; and the new connected-vs-disconnected wording split in `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` branch.
searchedFor: Grep button|click|rejected by the server|Turn on for later|offerOffline|setOfflinePersistenceEnabled in tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx

samples.summary: `reportLoss` is never exercised: nothing tests that a dropped-changes event flips the chip out of `saved-locally`
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` fires `local-changes-dropped` and spies only `store.expectLoss` (grep for `reportLoss|DurableLossWatch` in that file: no matches). `use-sync-status.test.ts` supplies `durable: false` through `DurableDocumentScope` by hand. So the link the design calls the one direction this feature must not fail in — SDK reports the local work was dropped → `reportLoss()` → context `durable:false` → chip stops promising the disk — is asserted at neither end together. A regression that latches `expectLoss` but forgets `reportLoss` leaves the chip reporting `Saved to this device` for work that is gone.

samples.summary: The Settings offline toggle and its `supportsClientKey()` gate have no test
samples.evidence: Grep for `offline-switch|Save documents on this device` across packages/frontend matches only `src/app/settings/page.tsx`; no settings page test file exists. The diff's comment states the gate is a rollout invariant ("the preference may land early because nothing reads it; the toggle may not"), because a switch on an unsupporting build promises storage and erasure that cannot happen. Nothing pins the gate, nor that `onCheckedChange` is wired to `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled`.
searchedFor: Grep offline-switch|Save documents on this device in packages/frontend

samples.summary: Nothing pins that the share route is wrapped in `NonDurableScope`
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` ('never persists anything reached through a share link') renders `NonDurableScope` itself, so it proves the scope works, not that `shared-document.tsx` uses it. The exclusion is positional by design (a share view of `sheet-7` has the same docKey as the owner's), so if the wrapper is dropped or moved below the provider during a refactor, a signed-in visitor's share view becomes durable — writing a shared document to disk past link revocation — and every existing test still passes.

samples.summary: The traversal assertion was weakened from every request to any request
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` for every URL a route function issued; it now asserts only `paths.some(...)`. The stated reason (deleteWorkspace's companion `fetchDocuments` call carries no id) is real, but the replacement no longer catches a second id-bearing request that encodes the id wrongly — it only needs one correctly-encoded URL among them. A narrower fix (exempt paths that contain no form of the id) would preserve the original property; as written the guard is weaker for every multi-request route, not just the new one.

finding.summary: `OfflineRuntime` — the whole housekeeping runtime — has no test of any kind
finding.evidence: Glob `packages/frontend/**/*offline-runtime*` returns only the source file; grep for `OfflineRuntime|offerRecoverableWork|rememberOfflineUser` across packages/frontend matches only offline-erase.ts/.test.ts (the helper), the component itself, and PrivateRoute.tsx. verdict.reason: Verified independently: `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx` is real orchestration (rememberOfflineUser on mount L53; WafflebaseDocStore L55-62; watchForOfflineDisable L67-70; collectStale L80; offerRecoverableWork L91 with cancelled-getter L130, unreadable-key skip L131-136, toast-id dedupe L149, getDocumentPath routing L179-183). No test anywhere exercises it. Repo-wide grep for `OfflineRuntime|offline-runtime` hits only the source, PrivateRoute.tsx:7,35, docs, and a prior review artifact. Grep for the orchestrated symbols hits only the lib sources and their own unit tests, which call the helpers directly and would keep passing if the component stopped invoking them. Searched outside src/ too: packages/frontend/tests/** has no offline files, there is no e2e dir, and no frontend *.spec.ts(x). Grep for the component's own user-facing strings ("Some changes could not be saved", "Save a copy", "offline-recovery-") matches only the component. The one test that renders full <App/> (app/templates/public-templates.test.tsx:88-101) deliberately rejects fetchMe (L94) so PrivateRoute redirects to /login and OfflineRuntime never mounts. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a regression in the mount-time rememberOfflineUser call silently leaves offline document content on a shared device after sign-out, and every offline-erase.test.ts case would still pass because those tests set the identity themselves.

finding.summary: The `eraseLocalData: false` guard on the 401 path — and `logout()`'s erase call — are untested
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` only covers 401 redirect de-duplication (grep for `erase|offline|401` returns lines 4-56, all about the redirect burst); no test in the repo asserts that the 401 arm of `fetchWithAuth` passes `eraseLocalData: false`. The diff's own comment states this is load-bearing: an involuntary expiry must not delete "the archives that hold changes the server never took", which are by design the only remaining copy of unreconciled work. A regression flipping that default destroys user work on a routine cookie expiry, and nothing would fail. Symmetrically, no test asserts `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` before redirecting, or that a failing erase cannot fail the sign-out — `offline-erase.test.ts` tests the helper in isolation, never the caller.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `auth.ts:121-123` gates the destructive erase on `eraseLocalData`, and `auth.ts:246-259` passes `eraseLocalData: false` on the 401 path. A repo-wide grep shows `eraseLocalData` occurs only in `src/api/auth.ts` and in no test file at all, and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` occurs only in `auth.ts`, `offline-erase.ts`, and `offline-erase.test.ts` (lines 250/266/273), where it is invoked directly as a unit, never through `logout()`. The sole `fetchWithAuth` 401 test (`tests/api/auth.test.ts:11-68`) asserts only on the `window.location.href` sequence for redirect de-duplication; flipping `eraseLocalData` to `true` would leave both of its tests passing. No indirect coverage exists: no test imports `logout` from `@/api/auth`; the only two tests importing `fetchWithAuth` (`image-upload.test.ts:3`, `image-insert.test.ts:3`) mock the whole `@/api/auth` module away; no test mocks or spies `@/lib/offline-erase`; and `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts:176-188`, despite its "on logout" title, calls `store.dropAllForUser` directly rather than the logout path. So the guard that prevents an involuntary expiry from deleting the only remaining copy of unreconciled work, and `logout()`'s await-before-redirect/never-fail-sign-out contract, have no test that could fail — a major, data-affecting missing-test gap under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `removeMember` gates the offline purge on `isOfflineUser(String(userId))` (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:137-138) and both it and `deleteWorkspace` call `documentIdsIn` before the DELETE (L115-120, L138-144). Repo-wide grep for `isOfflineUser` yields only its definition (lib/offline-erase.ts:101) and that single call site — no test references it. The two test files that touch these functions do not cover the behavior: url.test.ts:100-101 invokes them but asserts only path-segment encoding (L155-174), and its own comment at L167 explicitly exempts the companion listing request from assertion, so neither the guard nor the call ordering is pinned (with no offline user recorded, the purge is a no-op and an inverted guard changes no assertion); workspace-settings.test.tsx:28-40 mocks the whole `@/api/workspaces` module so the real body never executes, asserting only mock arguments at L203. offline-erase.test.ts:277-314 covers the `purgeOfflineDocuments` primitive (key scoping, archive retention, signed-out no-op) but never the caller-side decision of whether to invoke it. Also checked api/documents.test.ts, all 25 offline-matching test files, packages/frontend/tests/api/*, and any e2e/spec files (only backend workspace.service.spec.ts, which is server-side). Impact is major: an inverted guard deletes this device's local copies including unsent archived work with no visible symptom, and a reordered listing silently makes the purge a no-op.

finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` line 133-145 is the only `deleteDocuments` case; it mocks `okJson({ deleted: ['a'] })` and asserts the URL, method, body and returned value — nothing about `purgeOfflineDocuments`. verdict.reason: Verified independently: `deleteDocuments` (documents.ts:210-216) deliberately purges only `result.deleted`, and `deleteDocument` (documents.ts:162-173) purges only inside the `response.ok` branch, both justified by a data-loss comment. No test exercises either rule. The sole `deleteDocuments` test (documents.test.ts:136-144) mocks `{deleted:["a"]}` for the request `["a"]`, so server-confirmed and requested ids are indistinguishable, and it asserts only URL/method/body/return value; `@/lib/offline-erase` is never mocked or asserted in that file. `deleteDocument` appears only at line 112 in an id-encoding test asserting URLs (115-124), never the ok-gating. Searched wide: repo-wide grep for `purgeOffline` yields only documents.ts, workspaces.ts, offline-erase.ts and offline-erase.test.ts; the latter (277-313) tests purgeOfflineDocuments in isolation (key scoping, archive retention, signed-out no-op) and never calls the delete APIs. Repo-wide grep for `deleteDocument(s)` shows documents.test.ts is the only frontend test importing them; other matches are backend NestJS specs and CLI. Tests mocking `@/api/documents` stub read paths only. A regression to `purgeOfflineDocuments(ids)` on a partial-failure response, or dropping the `ok` guard, destroys unsent local work with the suite green — a data-affecting gap, major under the missing-tests branch.
